previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and a history of diabetic foot ulcers was admitted for hyperglycemia and fever. She had recently left the ED against medical advice but returned after her blood sugar exceeded 800 mg/dL. Evaluation revealed exposed calcaneal bone and gas on imaging, concerning for osteomyelitis. She was started on IV Vancomycin, Cefepime, and Flagyl. Vascular surgery recommended a below-the-knee amputation due to poor perfusion, but the patient opted to return home to consider the decision. She was discharged on oral Ciprofloxacin and Metronidazole, with continued Vancomycin during dialysis. Her blood glucose was stabilized on her home insulin regimen, and she received Nystatin for oral thrush. She was instructed to perform intermittent straight catheterization and to follow up with podiatry and vascular surgery for surgical planning.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with T1DM c/b neuropathy & gastroparesis, ESRD (___ HD), 
CAD, CHF, atrial fibrillation, and diabetic foot ulcers here 
after an episode of hypoglycemia, associated weakness, 
myoclonus, and hyponatremia.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Myoclonus:
# Involuntary Jerks: 
Myoclonic jerks appeared to be predominantly upper extremities 
and torso. This could happen in setting of hypoglycemia though 
hypoglycemia was transient and resolved though with ongoing 
myoclonus. New medications included Cipro, Flagyl, Vancomycin at 
HD (last trough ok). She has been on Gabapentin for a long time 
thought this was thought to be another potential culprit.  On 
admission, Cipro and Gabapentin were held.  She was started on 
Cefepime in place of Cipro for continued treatment of her foot 
infection.  Dilaudid was used sparingly for pain control.  Her 
electrolytes were corrected through HD.  By time of discharge 
patient was no longer experiencing the myoclonic jerks. 
Myoclonus thought related to Ciprofloxacin given acute onset 
after starting the medication and resolution after 
discontinuation.
   
# Hyponatremia: Patient with Na 125 in ED, mentating well. SOsm 
273 (low-normal), urine lytes with Na 34 UOsm 287 but difficult 
to interpret in the setting of ESRD. On exam, she appeared 
slightly volume overloaded and patient due for dialysis so 
likely hypervolemic hypernatremia.  Post HD her sodium was noted 
to be 132 which is far closer to her baseline. 
    
# Urinary retention
# Dirty UA: Patient with possible UTI on admission though did 
not endorse urinary symptoms at this time. Was given Linezolid 
in ED for concern of VRE UTI. Had Yeast in prior urine culture. 
Urine culture was mixed genital flora.  She did not receive 
further specific treatment for UTI this admission and remained 
stable.  Patient should get regular straight caths given 
recurrent very resistant UTIs, her risk of UTI is great.  She 
will be seen by Urology as an outpatient for further 
recommendations.  
   
# Diabetic Foot Ulcer with superimposed infection: 
# Osteomyelitis of foot: presumed
Patient with ongoing L calcaneal infection open to bone. On last 
admission, initially placed on Vanc/Cefepime/Flagyl switched to 
Vanc/Cipro/Flagyl on discharge. Patient was seen by ID this 
admission and switched to Ceftazidime and Vanc with HD and 
ongoing treatment with Flagyl. Team rediscussed BKA as 
definitive treatment for diabetic foot ulcer and potential 
osteomyelitis though she refused intervention while inpatient, 
this is consistent with prior discussions. Patietn indicated she 
knows she needs BKA for definitive therapy and indicated she is 
considering the operation but will complete as an outpatient. 
Patient will continue discussions with Podiatry/Vascular surgery 
regarding BKA for definitive treatment. 
     
CHRONIC ISSUES:
# T1DM: Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, Type I, complicated 
by retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, gastroparesis. Patient 
with brittle diabetes, most recent admitted for hyperglycemia 
FSBG >600 but with also reucrrent episodes of hypoglycemia. 
Decreased morning Lantus to 25units given lower blood sugars 
this admission.  She ultimately resumed her home dose of 
Gabapentin 100mg TID without any issue.
   
# ESRD on HD: HD schedule normally MWF through tunneled HD line. 
 She continued HD, Sevelamer, Nephrocaps, Omeprazole. She will 
need an AV graft and transplant surgery saw her while in house. 
However, transplant uncomfortable placing an AV graft in setting 
of active infection. As a result she will likely require BKA 
before an AV graft can be placed. This was discussed with 
patient who understands.
   
# CAD: Stable without active chest pain.  She continued home 
meds including ASA, Lisinopril, Carvedilol, Imdur and Hydrazine. 

  
# Hypothyroidism: Stable. Continued home levothyroxine 25mcg 
daily
 
# HFpEF: Patient likely with hypervolemic hyponatremia as can 
happen in setting of need for HD. She was dialyzed as above. 
  
# pAF: Off warfarin given concern for calciphylaxis, which per 
Derm is not consistent. Given CHADS2VASC score of 5, would

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure participating in your care at ___ 
___. You were admitted because 
uncontrollable twitching and low blood sugars.  While you were 
here we worked you up for any other infections beyond your foot 
and you did not have a urinary tract infection.  Your 
antibiotics were switched to IV antibiotics because we thought 
that Ciprofloxacin might have caused the twitching.  You went to 
dialysis as scheduled and did well. 

Again, you were seen by the podiatry team, the Vascular team and 
the Infectious Disease team. There was sufficient concern that 
your heel is not improving with conservative management and all 
of your doctors have recommended that you get a below the knee 
amputation of the left leg for definitive treatment as there are 
no other options to help your leg heal.  You should follow up 
with Dr. ___ Dr. ___ to discuss further plans for 
your ulcer. 

Dr. ___ should contact you with an appointment.  If you 
do not hear from them in the next couple of days, please call 
___ to schedule an appointment.  

When you leave the hospital, you will continue to get IV 
antibiotics at dialysis.  You will continue to take Flagyl by 
mouth in addition to these IV antibiotics.  

You should continue to have your visiting nurse straight cath 
you every other day to ensure you do not develop a urinary 
infection.  You have an appointment with a Urologist Dr. ___ 
___ below.  He will be able to provide further 
recommendations on your urologic care moving forwards. 

Weigh yourself every morning, call your doctor if weight goes up 
more than 3 lbs.

We wish you the best.

Sincerely,
Your ___ Team
